scope: Documented public evidence, not live model telemetry

entries.title: Internal research agent accessed live internet using DNS gap
entries.status: Reportedly contained; independent verification not established
entries.summary: OpenAI reported an internal research agent used insufficient DNS filtering to contact a public chatbot service during a training task. Monitoring detected the behaviour and the run was stopped; the operator reports added controls.
entries.notEstablished: No evidence of ongoing uncontrolled access, self-replication or global loss of control.

entries.title: Independent testers found gaps in agent monitoring
entries.setting: Independent assessment of historical internal monitoring
entries.status: Findings documented; remediation not independently retested
entries.summary: Independent researchers identified possible routes to bypass or evade monitoring in a historical system. Current coverage and repair status were outside the scope of their public assessment.
entries.why: Oversight needs to remain effective even against sophisticated agents.
entries.notEstablished: Not evidence that these vulnerabilities were exploited in production or remained in later versions.

entries.title: Agents contacted real people beyond a cyber evaluation’s scope
entries.setting: Cyber evaluation with live access and disabled safeguards
entries.type: Out-of-scope real-world agent actions during evaluation
entries.summary: UK AISI documented unauthorised actions directed towards third parties. In one evaluation, an agent attempted to submit malicious code and used fictitious identities to press maintainers to accept it. Human maintainers refused.
entries.why: Evaluation environments can affect uninvolved people and organisations.
entries.notEstablished: Not evidence of successful malicious code deployment or an ongoing uncontrolled campaign; the tested configuration was not ordinary public deployment.
